# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER
## Arabic Listening Pod (15 Scenes)

**TRANSLITERATION**
سارة = Sarah | جيمس = James | آنا = Anna | مانتشستر = Manchester | لندن = London | فرنسا = France | ديفيز = Davies | جونز = Jones

**PRICES**
- 8 pound 40 → مية وعشرين جنيه (one hundred twenty pounds)
- 12 pound 50 → ثلاثمية وخمسين جنيه (three hundred fifty pounds)

**TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME**
اللغة العربية (el-logha el-arabiyya) — colloquial short form: عربي (arabi)

**RECURRING LINES**
- "Good morning" → صباح الخير (sabah el-khair) [Scenes 1, 7, 12]
- "Good afternoon" → مساء الخير (masaa el-khair) [Scenes 3, 11]
- "Good evening" → مساء الخير (masaa el-khair) [Scenes 4, 5, 8, 9]
- "What can I get you?" → عايز/عايزة إيه؟ (ayez/ayza eh?) [Scenes 3, 7, 8]
- "See you later/then" → شوفك بعدين / شوفك كمان (shoufak ba'dayn / shoufak kaman) [Scenes 1, 4]
- "Could I pay by card?" → ممكن أدفع بكارت؟ (momken adfa' be-kart?) [Scenes 7, 14]
- "Of course" → بالطبع / تمام (bel-tabe' / tamam) [Scenes 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15]
- "Thank you very much" → شكراً كتير (shukran kteer) [Scenes 3, 13, 15]
- "Goodbye" → مع السلامة (ma'a el-salama) [Scenes 3, 10]
- "Would you like to sit-in or takeaway?" → عايز تشرب هنا ولا تاخده معاك؟ (ayez teshrub hena wala takhdo ma'ak?) [Scenes 3, 7]
- "Yes, I'm on holiday" → أيوه، أنا في إجازة (aywa, ana fi egaza) [Scenes 10, 15]
- "I'm learning Arabic" → أنا بتعلم عربي (ana bata'allem arabi) [Scenes 6, 10]
- "You speak very good Arabic" → أنت بتتكلم عربي كويس قوي (enta bettakallam arabi kwayyes qawi) [Scene 10]

**REGISTER**
- **Customer–Service staff** (barista, pharmacist, shop assistant, hotel receptionist, taxi driver): warm, moderately formal; use أنت (inta/inti) naturally; staff address customers with حضرتك (hadretak/hadretik) or by situation-appropriate title (آنسة anesa for young woman, أستاذ ustaz for man of any age); no elaborate ceremony, direct and helpful tone.
- **Strangers meeting socially** (introductions, tourist directions): polite but accessible; أنت unmarked; titles optional unless explicitly named profession (nurse, teacher).
- **Friends and peers** (Scene 15 learner–friend dialogue): أنت natural throughout; warm, encouraging, no formality markers.
- **Neighbours** (morning/evening greetings): warm, direct; أنت natural; term of address by name or simple كيف حالك (kif halak, how are you).
